answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a small refundable stake that only unlocks after a history of verified, useful work, like a vine that must grow along a terrace before it bears fruit. Creating one fake identity is cheap, but farming thousands means locking capital and time for each one, while slashing punishes bad work. An attacker who splits effort across many shells ends up with weak, unproven histories, whereas a single honest agent, tended like one walnut tree, accumulates trust that cannot be copied by cloning its name.
